doc.title: James Moody interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998

title: Race and jazz, and a book being written about him
summary: He rejects the idea that Negroes play jazz better; mentions Ursula Davis writing a book about his life.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Dizzy was a Bahai, yes. But he didn’t tell me anything about it. After he passed, my wife and I we became Bahais — because we would go to the chapel where we went, and for that very same reason the minister would be talking about, and Jesus said do good, and Jesus said do this, and he said be good and don’t do this. But he wouldn’t really say what should be said. Like you shouldn’t like hate a person and you shouldn’t teach your children to hate because you think that this is that and whatever. No they didn’t do that. Oh and another thing, in all the schools see, now they come up with that race thing about jazz. I was in France and the French were saying oh yes, well you know that the Negro plays jazz better than the Caucasian man. That isn’t true. It’s not true. Because all people are the same. And if you’ve got the ability, and you hear the music, and you like it, and you study it, you can play it. You can’t play a record and tell me who’s playing. You can’t play a record and tell me what color anyone is. Just like you can’t take some blood and tell me what color someone is. So I mean there are so many discrepancies in the world and the way people think. People think that if I look a certain way I’m better than you automatically. Stupid.
Sounds like you ought to write a book, to me.

Well a book is being written about me, by Nathan Davis’ wife, Dr. Ursula Davis. She’s writing a book about my life supposedly. But you know what I like? I would really like for people, like sometimes when you put it like in so-called black and white, people still don’t want to see what you know— I guess the actions speak louder than words. But jazz
